The 60-minute lesson on O3 is written: `lessons/0001-context-and-memory-in-an-agent.html`. I couldn't run a word count (the shell was blocked), so I haven't confirmed it falls in the 5,400–13,500 word range FORMATS.md accepts for 60 minutes. By my own estimate it lands at about 6,000 words, close to the lower edge.

The lesson opens with the win and an outline, then covers:
- **Context window:** what is in it on one call, and why a new tool costs tokens on every call.
- **Cost and context rot:** why a bigger window isn't free, with a cost sketch that uses made-up token counts.
- **Between steps:** the program resends the transcript on every step, and old tool results can be cleared or compacted.
- **Between sessions:** memory is storage your code writes and reads, so decide what to save and what to leave out.
- **Retrieval:** chunking, embeddings and keyword search, and when pasting all the manuals is an option.
- **Practice and review:** a booking request worked in six small steps, two practice tasks with the steps faded, and a list of design-review questions.

Every claim is cited to Anthropic's posts on context engineering, context management and contextual retrieval. I opened all three, and the lesson links to them with the context-engineering post as the primary source.

I also added `RESOURCES.md` and a one-page `cheatsheets/context-and-memory.html`, and updated `NOTES.md`. Because the lesson alone isn't evidence of learning, I wrote no learning record. When you're ready, ask for a quiz on it with `/quiz`, and ask me anything about the lesson in the chat.

Questions for you:
- Do you want a community recommendation for testing this in the real world? I left it out because I haven't asked you before.
